title: A small maths library
description:
Write a library of functions that call each other, all following the System V convention. The tests call every function and check that `rbx`, `rbp` and `r12` to `r15` come back unchanged.

| Function | Result |
|---|---|
| `gcd(a, b)` | the greatest common divisor of two numbers >= 0, **recursively**: gcd(a, 0) = a, otherwise gcd(b, a mod b) |
| `lcm(a, b)` | the least common multiple, a / gcd(a, b) × b, calling `gcd`; lcm with a 0 is 0 |
| `is_prime(n)` | 1 if n is prime, else 0 (try divisors d while d × d <= n) |
| `nth_prime(k)` | the kth prime, k >= 1: nth_prime(1) is 2; calls `is_prime` |
| `insertion_sort(array, n)` | sorts an array of signed 8-byte numbers in place, smallest first |
| `median(array, n)` | sorts the array (calling `insertion_sort`) and returns the middle element, or for an even n the lower of the two middle ones |
| `binary_search(array, n, value)` | in a sorted array, the index of value, or −1; **recursive** on the half that can hold it, through a helper that takes the low and high bounds |

starter.solution.asm:
gcd:
        mov     rax, rdi
        ret

lcm:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

is_prime:
        xor     eax, eax
        ret

nth_prime:
        mov     eax, 2
        ret

insertion_sort:
        ret

median:
        mov     rax, [rdi]
        ret

binary_search:
        mov     rax, -1
        ret

solution.solution.asm:
; gcd: rdi = a, rsi = b (both >= 0). Returns their greatest common divisor.
gcd:
        test    rsi, rsi
        jnz     .recurse
        mov     rax, rdi
        ret
.recurse:
        sub     rsp, 8                  ; keep the stack aligned for the call
        mov     rax, rdi
        xor     edx, edx
        div     rsi                     ; rdx = a mod b
        mov     rdi, rsi
        mov     rsi, rdx
        call    gcd
        add     rsp, 8
        ret

; lcm: rdi = a, rsi = b. Returns their least common multiple (0 if either is 0).
lcm:
        xor     eax, eax
        test    rdi, rdi
        jz      .done
        test    rsi, rsi
        jz      .done
        push    rbx
        push    r12
        sub     rsp, 8
        mov     rbx, rdi
        mov     r12, rsi
        call    gcd
        mov     rcx, rax
        mov     rax, rbx
        xor     edx, edx
        div     rcx                     ; a / gcd
        imul    rax, r12                ; * b
        add     rsp, 8
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
.done:  ret

; is_prime: rdi = n. Returns 1 if n is prime, else 0.
is_prime:
        xor     eax, eax
        cmp     rdi, 2
        jl      .done
        mov     ecx, 2
.try:   mov     rax, rcx
        imul    rax, rcx
        cmp     rax, rdi
        ja      .prime                  ; d * d > n: no divisor found
        mov     rax, rdi
        xor     edx, edx
        div     rcx
        test    rdx, rdx
        jz      .not_prime
        inc     rcx
        jmp     .try
.prime: mov     eax, 1
        ret
.not_prime:
        xor     eax, eax
.done:  ret

; nth_prime: rdi = k >= 1. Returns the kth prime.
nth_prime:
        push    rbx                     ; the candidate
        push    r12                     ; primes still to find
        sub     rsp, 8
        mov     r12, rdi
        mov     ebx, 1
.next:  inc     rbx
        mov     rdi, rbx
        call    is_prime
        test    rax, rax
        jz      .next
        dec     r12
        jnz     .next
        mov     rax, rbx
        add     rsp, 8
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret

; insertion_sort: rdi = array of signed 8-byte numbers, rsi = count. Sorts it in place.
insertion_sort:
        mov     ecx, 1
.outer: cmp     rcx, rsi
        jae     .done
        mov     r8, [rdi + rcx*8]       ; the element to insert
        mov     rdx, rcx
.shift: test    rdx, rdx
        jz      .place
        mov     r9, [rdi + rdx*8 - 8]
        cmp     r9, r8
        jle     .place
        mov     [rdi + rdx*8], r9       ; move the bigger one up
        dec     rdx
        jmp     .shift
.place: mov     [rdi + rdx*8], r8
        inc     rcx
        jmp     .outer
.done:  ret

; median: rdi = array, rsi = count >= 1. Sorts the array and returns the (lower) middle element.
median:
        push    rbx
        push    r12
        sub     rsp, 8
        mov     rbx, rdi
        mov     r12, rsi
        call    insertion_sort
        lea     rax, [r12 - 1]
        shr     rax, 1                  ; (n - 1) / 2
        mov     rax, [rbx + rax*8]
        add     rsp, 8
        pop     r12
        pop     rbx
        ret

; binary_search: rdi = sorted array, rsi = count, rdx = value. Returns its index or -1.
binary_search:
        mov     rcx, rsi                ; high (one past the end)
        xor     esi, esi                ; low
        jmp     search_range

; search_range: rdi = array, rsi = low, rcx = high (exclusive), rdx = value.
search_range:
        cmp     rsi, rcx
        jb      .look
        mov     rax, -1
        ret
.look:  lea     rax, [rsi + rcx]
        shr     rax, 1                  ; the middle
        mov     r8, [rdi + rax*8]
        cmp     r8, rdx
        je      .found                  ; rax is the index
        jl      .upper
        mov     rcx, rax                ; the value is in the lower half
        jmp     .recurse
.upper: lea     rsi, [rax + 1]          ; the upper half
.recurse:
        sub     rsp, 8                  ; (sub changes the flags, so it comes after the jumps)
        call    search_range
        add     rsp, 8
.found: ret

requirements: `gcd` and the binary search are recursive.
`lcm`, `nth_prime` and `median` call the other functions rather than repeating their code.
Every function saves the callee-saved registers it uses, and keeps `rsp` aligned to 16 at each call it makes.
A comment above each function says what goes in and what comes out.
